newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina launches wheat quality drive.
newsitem.headline: Argentina launches wheat quality drive.

text.p: Argentina's Agriculture Secretary Felipe Sola announced on Thursday a government drive for the country's wheat producers to upgrade their marketing techniques and sell their product according to improved quality scales.

"I want to create a long-term wheat policy," he told a seminar on wheat quality, adding that challenges included creating the mechanisms for "exporters to sell different qualities of wheat at different prices."
An issue to be addressed is deciding how the nation's grain storage facilities can be modified to handle marketing of a revamped range of separate wheat qualities.
Argentina must develop "a brand and a clear identity for its wheat," Sola said.
One of the government's objectives is to create a new, high quality grade to be known as "silver", or "plata" in Spanish, wheat, but its precise characteristics have still to be determined.
Sola's comments come after the formation recently of a new farmers' association to promote improvements in wheat classification and marketing.

The farmers want to replace the present system of classifying wheat according to just three quality levels with a more complicated system of grades differentiating milling properties such as protein level and specific weight.
Argentine wheat is presently jumbled into storage and ships with little regard for differences of quality, putting the country at a marketing disadvantage to slicker competitors such as Canada.

The Argentine Wheat Producers Association sent a delegation to met Sola, who received them enthusiastically and told them he wanted to put a new quality stamp system in place before the 1997/98 harvest.
Sola said Thursday he also wanted to investigate ways to encourage Argentine flour exports, which are now just a tiny percentage of wheat exports.
